gaps.sentence: There was a lot of ___ (OPPOSE) to the new road.
gaps.explanation: 'A lot of' needs a noun: opposition (-tion noun); 'opposite' is an adjective or noun meaning the contrary.

gaps.sentence: In my opinion, that restaurant is ___ — the food is nothing special (RATE).
gaps.explanation: 'Nothing special' shows the restaurant is praised too much: overrated (over- + rated).

gaps.sentence: The train arrived ___ , despite the snow (PUNCTUAL).
gaps.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify 'arrived': punctually (-ly). 'Punctuality' is the noun.

gaps.sentence: The old factory will be ___ into flats (MODERN).
gaps.hint: verb needed in the passive (-ise); past participle
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ise forms the verb: modernise. The passive 'will be' needs the past participle 'modernised'.

gaps.sentence: Try to be ___ when you cross the busy road (CARE).
gaps.explanation: An adjective is needed after 'be': careful (-ful). 'Carefully' is an adverb and cannot follow 'be'.
After 'in' a noun is needed: excitement (-ment noun).

gaps.sentence: It is ___ to book tickets in advance during the festival (ADVICE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -able forms the adjective: advisable means worth recommending. 'It is + adjective + to-infinitive'.
